bluf: Brave Bison is a European enterprise media, marketing and technology company whose record leads with creators (a YouTube network, fan engagement, the Alofoke live stream case) and SEO, with GEO, digital PR, paid media and commerce builds behind. It is selling AI search hard: a GEO page for AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity, AudienceGPT and AdStudio in its nav, LinkedIn ads on citations. Its one dated 2026 move adds Racing TV on YouTube. What a rival should know: the house contradicts the pitch, no llms.txt and nothing updated in 12 months, and Google, SharkNinja, Currys, Icelandair, Beats by Dre and PGA Tour all sit on other tracked books.
doing:
The positioning line reads: media, marketing and technology company built for the digital era, spanning organic and paid performance, commerce technology, social, fan engagement and a creator media network: a search and social agency bolted to a YouTube channel business and an ecommerce build shop. The headline claim is 300+ ecommerce projects and £3bn in transactions plus a record setting YouTube live stream for Alofoke, whose case claims the most viewed live stream in YouTube history at 700m views; the rest is a claim.

Service lines run from Organic and Paid Performance through Technology & Experience, Social & Influencer, Fan Engagement and Digital Media Network to GEO, Digital PR, Programmatic Display, Paid Social and CRO. It leads with Creator & Influencer and SEO, both scored 3: the creator line carries the YouTube network and the SharkNinja, BBC TikTok and Montblanc cases; the SEO line the Currys migration and the Very, Aviva and Vitality cases. Core lines scored 2 are AI Search (the GEO page), Content & Digital PR (Avis £948k and Fairmont $1m media value cases), Paid Search (Furniture Village ROAS up 150%), Programmatic & CTV (New Balance £1.7m incremental revenue) and Web & Product (builds for MKM and Winparts). Partners are commerce platforms (Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Adobe Commerce, BigCommerce, Shopify, SAP, Bloomreach); AudienceGPT and AdStudio are proprietary labels known from the nav alone. Data & Measurement, Email & CRM, B2B, local and retail media all score 0.

Its AI posture is GEO for AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity plus an AI search maturity framework; its director of AI and creative was quoted by Digiday on ChatGPT ads in May 2025. The one dated move is 2026: Racing TV added as a YouTube channel management client at Cheltenham Festival 2026. Pricing: the Paid Performance page says it only wins when clients win, an outcome hint, no prices. Absent: an owned audience line, news, jobs, offices, ownership and a founding date.
clients:
The client type is enterprise, across sport, retail and ecommerce, travel and hospitality, media and entertainment, insurance and financial services, consumer technology and health and wellbeing; the region is Europe, no office or owner listed.

The needs read holds 16 clients, 8 observed and 8 names only; organic demand leads the mix. Currys came for organic and web work (page one keyword visibility up 4,000% after migration), Specsavers for global and AI search visibility, Icelandair for search visibility with digital PR. SharkNinja came for a CryoGlow influencer campaign, Beats by Dre for a World Cup social campaign, Amazon Prime Video for a TikTok creator series. New Balance came for London Marathon paid media (15% sales growth); Furniture Village codes commerce from its slug, though the paid search note credits it with ROAS up 150%.

The 8 names only are Aviva, Warner Bros., Arsenal FC, Google, BBC, The Very Group, ICC and PGA Tour, their need inferred from creators and SEO, its lead lines. Some carry uncoded evidence: the SEO note credits Aviva and Very with technical SEO cases, the creator note a BBC TikTok case, and the PGA Tour title reads YouTube revenue up 107%.

Six sit on other tracked books: Google (huge, instrument, r-ga, dept, media-monks, akqa), SharkNinja (ayima, peak-ace), Currys (epsilon), Icelandair (builtvisible), Beats by Dre (pmg) and PGA Tour (mindgruve).

Specsavers shows the book buying AI search visibility under KJ1, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that retail and travel accounts ask next for audited citation measurement, which P1 partial says it lacks. With KJ8 (human provenance as a distribution signal) its best placed judgment, creator and YouTube work likely holds; Data & Measurement at 0 against the KJ9 headwind makes it likely the paid accounts need a measurement partner it is not.
house:
Say and do: four lines tested, two practised, integrity 50. AI Search / GEO is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt. Publishing cadence is contradicted: a blog exists but nothing in the sitemap has updated for 12 months, 0 URLs updated in 90 and 365 days against 552 listed, the case study entries carrying empty lastmod fields. Paid Search is corroborated: 2 Google ads of its own, 2 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-27. Creator & Influencer is corroborated: its own Instagram and TikTok channels are linked from the site.

The stack is GTM and the LinkedIn Insight pixel on Gatsby with Contentful; no test tools, no ABM stack, no AI crawlers blocked. LinkedIn is active at 21+ ads (19 company page, 2 thought leader, the count a floor); a sample reads: AI tools don't cite content that ranks once and fades. Meta and TikTok: the record is silent.
market:
Horus reads 15.5, band Favored. Best placed for KJ8, human provenance becomes a distribution signal (net 0.284, Creator & Influencer and Content & Digital PR), and KJ1, the click is being replaced by the citation (net 0.23, AI Search / GEO). Most exposed to KJ9, measurement gets worse before it gets better (net minus 0.138, SEO), and KJ5, the price of attention splits in two. The mix sits at 16:14 on the Solar Arc; best fit is The Toll Road at 45/100. It is making P5 (outcome pricing on its own pages), partial on P1 (audited AI visibility), P4 (no first party data or measurement depth behind its paid media) and P8 (no holdout capability), absent on P2, P6 and P7; P3 does not apply.

The Monsoon read is 46.9, Breeze: migration 51.9 against displacement 41.9, SEO (14) and Web & Product (10) carrying the most movable hours. Shore: 50% South and Southeast Asia, 40% Eastern Europe. The evidence class is observed, an outcome term pulling the index down; no hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the say and do gap on AI search: it sells GEO for AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity, runs LinkedIn ads on AI citations, and publishes no llms.txt while its own sitemap has not updated in 12 months. A rival showing a live publishing cadence and an audited citation share (P1 is partial here) is likely, moderate confidence, to beat it on its own pitch. Falsifier: an llms.txt on bravebison.com and fresh sitemap dates.

Second, the shared book: Google sits on the huge, instrument, r-ga, dept, media-monks and akqa books, and SharkNinja, Currys, Icelandair, Beats by Dre and PGA Tour each on at least one more, so those accounts already shop, contestable at roughly even chance each. Third, measurement: Data & Measurement scores 0, P4 is partial and KJ9 is its main headwind, so an offer led by incrementality and holdouts on paid media undercuts the New Balance and SharkNinja style work; likely, moderate confidence. Fourth, P2 is absent: no feed, schema or entity work despite the commerce builds, unclaimed ground. Price is not the lever: Monsoon reads Breeze at 46.9 with an observed outcome pricing term, so an offshore undercut is unlikely to bite.
watch: Indicator I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, reads 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas would strengthen KJ8, its best placed judgment, and test the creator network.
Indicator I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, reads late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization and sharpens the KJ1 tailwind behind its GEO line.
Indicator I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, reads late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
Indicator I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, is rolling: pricing below $20 CPM bears on P8, where it talks ads inside assistants with no holdout capability shown.
Follow up the 2026 Racing TV YouTube move and whether AudienceGPT and AdStudio become described products rather than nav labels.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
